0188:   def toposort(self, gate:Callable|None=None, enter_calls=True) -> dict[UOp, None]:
0189:     cache: dict[UOp, None] = {}
0190:     stack: list[tuple[UOp, bool]] = [(self, False)] # each stack entry is (node, visited_flag)
0191:     while stack:
0192:       node, visited = stack.pop()
0193:       if node in cache: continue
0194:       if not visited:
0195:         if gate is None or gate(node):
0196:           stack.append((node, True))  # push node back on stack to process after its srcs
0197:           for s in reversed(node.src if enter_calls or node.op not in {Ops.CALL, Ops.FUNCTION} else node.src[1:]):
0198:             stack.append((s, False)) # push srcs on the stack
0199:       else: cache[node] = None # second time i'm seeing this node, add it to returned toposort
0200:     return cache

0011: def check_uop_against_string(self, v:UOp, s:str):
0012:   sym_vars = {v.render():v for v in v.toposort() if v.op in (Ops.RANGE, Ops.SPECIAL, Ops.PARAM)}
0013:   s_eval = eval(s, sym_vars)
0014:   if isinstance(s_eval, int) and v.dtype==dtypes.weakint: s_eval = UOp.const(dtypes.weakint, s_eval)
0015:   elif isinstance(s_eval, (bool, int, float)): s_eval = UOp.const(dtypes.from_py(s_eval), s_eval)
0016:   s_eval = graph_rewrite(s_eval, commutative, name="cannonicalize eval")
0017:   self.assertIs(s_eval, v, f"eval did not match simplified: {s_eval} != {v.render()} for {s}")

0296:   def test_matmul(self):
0297:     a = Tensor.randn(10,10)
0298:     b = Tensor.randn(10,10)
0299:     c = Tensor.empty(10,10)
0300:     ref = (a@b)
0301:     with Context(DEBUG=0): Tensor.realize(a, b, c, ref)
0302: 
0303:     # C[i,j] = sum_k A[i,k] * B[k,j]
0304:     # Shapes: A[M,K], B[K,N], C[M,N]
0305:     M = N = K = 10
0306:     DT = dtypes.float32
0307: 
0308:     # Placeholders (bind slots explicitly)
0309:     A = UOp.placeholder((M, K), DT, slot=0)
0310:     B = UOp.placeholder((K, N), DT, slot=1)
0311:     C = UOp.placeholder((M, N), DT, slot=2)
0312: 
0313:     # Axes: i,j are spatial; k is a reduction axis over the shared dim K
0314:     i = UOp.range(M, axis_id=0)                             # rows of A/C
0315:     j = UOp.range(N, axis_id=1)                             # cols of B/C
0316:     k = UOp.range(K, axis_id=2, axis_type=AxisType.REDUCE)  # reduction over K
0317: 
0318:     # Zero-init: write a scalar 0 to each (i,j).
0319:     C = C[i, j].set(0.0)
0320: 
0321:     # Accumulate: C_after(k) enforces the dependency along the reduction axis
0322:     C = C[i, j].set(C.after(k)[i, j] + A[i, k] * B[k, j])
0323: 
0324:     # Finalize the loop nest / schedule in (i, j, k) order
0325:     prog = C.end(i, j, k)
0326: 
0327:     # run program
0328:     # TODO: make this work with opts_to_apply
0329:     self._run(prog.sink(arg=KernelInfo(opts_to_apply=())), a, b, c)

0508:   def test_walk_bidirectional_bpm_short_circuits(self):
0509:     """If bpm matches, children are skipped and pm never fires on that node."""
0510:     visited = []
0511:     def bpm_match(ctx, x):
0512:       ctx.append((x.arg if x.op is Ops.CONST else x.op, "bpm"))
0513:       # rewrite const(1) -> const(10), short-circuiting its subtree
0514:       if x.op is Ops.CONST and x.arg == 1: return x.replace(arg=10)
0515:       return None
0516:     def pm_match(ctx, x):
0517:       ctx.append((x.arg if x.op is Ops.CONST else x.op, "pm"))
0518:       return None
0519:     bpm = PatternMatcher([(UPat(GroupOp.All, name="x"), bpm_match)])
0520:     pm = PatternMatcher([(UPat(GroupOp.All, name="x"), pm_match)])
0521:     a = UOp.const(dtypes.int, 1)
0522:     b = UOp.const(dtypes.int, 2)
0523:     ret = graph_rewrite(a + b, pm, ctx=visited, bpm=bpm, walk=True)
0524:     # bpm matches const(1) and short-circuits it, so pm never fires on const(1)
0525:     self.assertNotIn((1, "pm"), visited)
0526:     # but pm still fires on const(2) and the rebuilt ADD
0527:     self.assertIn((2, "pm"), visited)

2790: class TestMin3Max3Unsigned(unittest.TestCase):
2791:   """Regression tests for V_MIN3/V_MAX3 with unsigned integer types.
2792: 
2793:   The emulator's _minmax_reduce used UOp.minimum() which implements min(a,b) as
2794:   -max(-a,-b). This is broken for unsigned types because negation (mul by -1)
2795:   doesn't preserve ordering: for uint16, -0 = 0 but -5 = 65531, so
2796:   max(-0, -5) = max(0, 65531) = 65531, and -65531 = 5, giving min(0,5) = 5 (wrong!).
2797: 
2798:   Fix: use comparison-based min/max for unsigned types: min(a,b) = (a<b)?a:b
2799:   """

0022: def apply_rope(x:Tensor, freqs_cis:Tensor) -> Tensor:
0023:   assert x.shape[-1] % 2 == 0
0024:   cos, sin = freqs_cis.reshape(1, 1, x.shape[2], -1).chunk(2, dim=-1)
0025:   x1, x2 = x.chunk(2, dim=-1)
0026:   return (x1 * cos - x2 * sin).cat(x2 * cos + x1 * sin, dim=-1)
0027: 
0028: def pairwise_topk(x: Tensor, k: int) -> tuple[Tensor, Tensor]:
0029:   n = x.shape[-1]
0030:   vals = Tensor.arange(n).reshape(1,1,n).cast(x.dtype).expand(x.shape)
0031:   cmp = (x.unsqueeze(-1) > x.unsqueeze(-2)) | ((x.unsqueeze(-1) == x.unsqueeze(-2)) & \
0032:     (Tensor.arange(n).reshape(1,1,n,1) < Tensor.arange(n).reshape(1,1,1,n)))
0033:   sel = x.const_like(0).scatter(-1, cmp.sum(axis=-1).cast('int32'), vals)[:,:,n-k:].cast('int32')
0034:   return x.gather(-1, sel), sel

0240:   def __init__(self, config:TransformerConfig, ssm:SSMConfig):
0241:     super().__init__(config)

0008: def _time_queue(q, d):
0009:   st = time.perf_counter()
0010:   q.signal(d.timeline_signal, d.timeline_value)
0011:   q.submit(d)
0012:   d._wait_signal(d.timeline_signal, d.timeline_value)
0013:   d.timeline_value += 1
0014:   return time.perf_counter() - st

0280: # vshufpd xmm2, xmm0, xmm1, imm
0281: # for 128 bit xmm2 selects its lower 64 bits from xmm0 and its upper 64 bits from xmm1 according to imm
0282: # for 256 bit ymm2 also selects its upper 128 bits from the upper 128 bits of ymm0 and ymm1 following the same constraint
0283: def vshufpd(x:UOp) -> UOp|None:
0284:   a, b = base(x, 0), base(x, 1)
0285:   if lane(x, 0) > 1 or lane(x, 1) > 1: return None
0286:   if len(x.src) == 4 and not (a is base(x, 2) and b is base(x, 3) and lane(x, 2) > 1 and lane(x, 3) > 1): return None
0287:   return x.ins(X86Ops.VSHUFPD, src=(a, b, imm(dtypes.uint8, sum(lane(x, i) << i for i in range(len(x.src))))))
0288:

0290: # inserts any 32 bit element in xmm1 into any position in xmm0 according to immm, result is written to xmm2
0291: # this is the fallback slow case for when you can't match more a powerful shuffle
0292: def vinsertps(x:UOp) -> UOp:
0293:   def _insert(ret:UOp, i:int) -> UOp:
0294:     s, v = base(x, i), lane(x, i)
0295:     # moving the 0th element into the 0th position does nothing
0296:     return s if i == v == 0 else x.ins(X86Ops.VINSERTPS, src=(ret, s, imm(dtypes.uint8, v << 6 | i << 4)))
0297:   return functools.reduce(_insert, range(len(x.src)), def_reg(x.dtype))

0299: # vpinsq xmm2, xmm0, rax, imm
0300: # inserts element in rax into any position in xmm0, result is written to xmm2 according to imm
0301: def vpins(x:UOp) -> UOp:
0302:   op = {1: X86Ops.VPINSRB, 2: X86Ops.VPINSRW, 4: X86Ops.VPINSRD, 8: X86Ops.VPINSRQ}[x.dtype.scalar().itemsize]
0303:   return functools.reduce(lambda ret,i: x.ins(op, src=(ret, x.src[i], imm(dtypes.uint8, i))), range(len(x.src)), def_reg(x.dtype))

0305: # vpbroadcastd xmm1, xmm0
0306: # inserts scalar int in xmm0 into all lanes of xmm1
0307: def vpbroadcast(ctx:IselContext, x:UOp, y:UOp) -> UOp:
0308:   n = x.ins({1: X86Ops.VPBROADCASTB, 2: X86Ops.VPBROADCASTW, 4: X86Ops.VPBROADCASTD, 8: X86Ops.VPBROADCASTQ}[y.dtype.itemsize], src=(y,))
0309:   if y.op is Ops.LOAD and len(y.src) == 1 and is_foldable(ctx, n, y): return n
0310:   # if there isn't a load we can fold we need to move y from gpr to xmm

0315: # we don't call ctx.vreg on the srcs to avoid duplicates, a rewrite will assign the tuple of valid registers to a vreg
0316: def idiv(ctx:IselContext, x:UOp) -> UOp:
0317:   op = X86Ops.DIV if x.dtype in dtypes.uints else X86Ops.IDIV
0318:   # for >8bit need to zero/sign extend rax to rdx
0319:   if x.dtype in dtypes.int8s: ext = []
0320:   elif x.dtype in dtypes.uints: ext = [x.ins(X86Ops.MOVi, src=(imm(min(dtypes.uint32, x.dtype), 0),), tag=(RDX,))]
0321:   else: ext = [x.ins(X86Ops.SARi, src=(x.src[0], imm(dtypes.uint8, x.dtype.itemsize * 8 - 1)), tag=(RDX,))]
0322:   # for 8bit need to zero/sign extend al to ah
0323:   if x.dtype is dtypes.uint8: dividend = UOp(Ops.INS, arg=X86Ops.MOVZX, dtype=dtypes.int16, src=(x.src[0],), tag=(RAX,))
0324:   elif x.dtype is dtypes.int8: dividend = UOp(Ops.INS, arg=X86Ops.MOVSX, dtype=dtypes.int16, src=(x.src[0],), tag=(RAX,))
0325:   else: dividend = x.ins(X86Ops.MOV, src=(x.src[0],), tag=(RAX,))
0326:   # divisor can't be in rax or rdx
0327:   divisor = x.ins(X86Ops.MOV, src=(x.src[1],), tag=tuple(r for r in WGPR if r not in (RAX, RDX)))
0328:   # for >8bit both rax and rdx are written to
0329:   defs = (ctx.vreg(RAX),) if x.dtype in dtypes.int8s else (ctx.vreg(RAX), ctx.vreg(RDX))
0330:   idiv = x.ins(op, src=(dividend, divisor) + tuple(ext), tag=defs)
0331:   # this move "cleanses" the register constraints (rax/rdx) of idiv as that only applies on definition and not on the uses of idiv
0332:   return x.ins(X86Ops.MOV, src=(idiv,))

0334: # a memory address operand is (base, index, displacement, size). size is the element size, it scales the index and is the memory operand width.
0335: # it is materialized as an immediate so the address stays correct if the base register is ever spilled and refilled
0336: def fold_address(x:UOp) -> tuple[UOp, UOp, UOp, UOp]:

0341:   # buffers are indexed by element, everything else (the stack pointer) by byte
0342:   scale = base.dtype.itemsize if base.op in {Ops.PARAM, Ops.BUFFER, Ops.AFTER} else 1
0343:   sz = imm(dtypes.uint8, base.dtype.itemsize)

0346:   return (base, _cast(idx), _disp(0), sz)

0362: def alloc_vregs(ctx:IselContext, x:UOp) -> UOp|None:

0614: # ***** pre register allocation *****
0615: # this handles flag clobbers. Unfortunately x86 doesn't have a good way to store/restore the flag register (then regalloc would handle it)
0616: # so we rematerialize. This is different from rematerialization you might want to do in regalloc because it is not optional,
0617: # regalloc shouldn't rematerialize if a src of the instruction is dead, but here you need to as there's no fallback load from stack
0618: def flag_rematerialize(ctx:PreRegAllocContext, x:UOp):
0619:   flag_def = x if x.arg in X86GroupOp.WriteFlags or x.op in (Ops.RANGE, Ops.END) else x.src[-1] if x.arg in X86GroupOp.ReadFlags else None
0620:   if flag_def is None: return None
0621:   if ctx.lock is not None and ctx.lock is not flag_def: ctx.clobbered.add(ctx.lock)
0622:   ctx.lock = flag_def
0623:   if flag_def not in ctx.clobbered: return None
0624:   ctx.clobbered.remove(flag_def)
0625:   return (x, [flag_def, x])
0626: 
0627: pre_regalloc_matcher = PatternMatcher([
0628:   (UPat((Ops.INS, Ops.RANGE, Ops.END), name="x"), flag_rematerialize),
0629: ])

0111: def _f32_to_bf16(v: UOp) -> UOp:
0112:   """Convert f32 to bf16 with round-to-nearest-even. BF16 is the upper 16 bits of F32 with rounding."""
0113:   bits = (v.bitcast(dtypes.float32) if v.dtype != dtypes.float32 else v).bitcast(dtypes.uint32)
0114:   # Round-to-nearest-even: add rounding bias. If the bit just below the truncation point is 1 and the rest are 0, round to even.
0115:   round_bit = (bits >> _u32(16)) & _u32(1)  # bit 16 (LSB of kept part)
0116:   rounding = _u32(0x7FFF) + round_bit  # 0x7FFF + bit16: rounds to even
0117:   rounded = bits + rounding
0118:   return (rounded >> _u32(16)).cast(dtypes.uint16)
0119: def _f32_to_bf16_sr(v: UOp, stoch: UOp) -> UOp:
0120:   """Convert f32 to bf16 with stochastic rounding."""
0121:   bits = (v.bitcast(dtypes.float32) if v.dtype != dtypes.float32 else v).bitcast(dtypes.uint32)
0122:   # Stochastic rounding: add lower 16 bits of stochastic value to lower 16 bits of f32
0123:   rounded = bits + (stoch & _u32(0xFFFF))
0124:   return (rounded >> _u32(16)).cast(dtypes.uint16)

0270: def _ff1(val: UOp, bits: int) -> UOp:

0279: def _sad_u8(a: UOp, b: UOp, acc: UOp, masked: bool = False) -> UOp:
0280:   """Sum of absolute differences of 4 unsigned bytes + accumulator. If masked, skips bytes where a == 0."""
0281:   a, b, acc = a.cast(dtypes.uint32), b.cast(dtypes.uint32), acc.cast(dtypes.uint32)

0284:     a_byte = (a >> _u32(i * 8)) & _u32(0xFF)

0288:   return result

0032: def fold_const_alu(a:UOp) -> UOp|None:
0033:   vals = [const_arg(s) for s in a.src]
0034:   return None if any(v is None for v in vals) else a.const_like(exec_alu(a.op, a.dtype, vals, False))

0036: def _quotient_base(q:UOp, base:UOp, div:int) -> UOp|None:
0037:   # the B with q == B//div and B%div == base%div, or None. only such congruence is needed to recombine, and canonicalization
0038:   # moves consts freely: the quotient may be merged ((x//c + a)//div -> (x + a*c)//(c*div) for div>0) and shifted ((y + k*D)//D == y//D + k)
0039:   (q, s), (num, a) = q.pop_const(), base.pop_const()
0040:   if q.op is not Ops.FLOORDIV or q.src[1].op is not Ops.CONST: return None
0041:   if div > 0 and num.op is Ops.FLOORDIV and num.src[1].op is Ops.CONST and q.src[1].arg == (c:=num.src[1].arg)*div: num, a, D = num.src[0], a*c, c*div
0042:   elif q.src[1].arg == div: D = div
0043:   else: return None
0044:   (x, xa), (p, pa) = num.pop_const(), q.src[0].pop_const()
0045:   if p is not x or (t:=xa + a - pa) % D: return None
0046:   return base - k*div if (k:=t//D - s) else base
0047: 
0048: def fold_add_divmod_recombine(x:UOp) -> UOp|None:
0049:   # a scaled mod (base%div)*mul recombines with a partner q*(div*mul) carrying the quotient of a b == base (mod div):
0050:   #   q == b//div     -> b*mul              (full recombine)
0051:   #   q == (b//div)%d -> (b%(div*d))*mul    (partial recombine into a wider mod, needs d>0)
0052:   terms = list(x.split_uop(Ops.ADD))
0053:   for i,u in enumerate(terms):
0054:     mod, mul = u.pop_const(Ops.MUL)
0055:     if mod.op is not Ops.FLOORMOD or mod.src[1].op is not Ops.CONST: continue
0056:     base, div = mod.src[0], mod.src[1].arg
0057:     for j,v in enumerate(terms):
0058:       q, scale = v.pop_const(Ops.MUL)
0059:       if i == j or scale != div*mul: continue
0060:       rest = [t for k,t in enumerate(terms) if k not in (i,j)]
0061:       if (b:=_quotient_base(q, base, div)) is not None: return (b*mul).usum(*rest)
0062:       if q.op is Ops.FLOORMOD and q.src[1].op is Ops.CONST and (d:=q.src[1].arg) > 0 and (b:=_quotient_base(q.src[0], base, div)) is not None:
0063:         return ((b % (div*d))*mul).usum(*rest)
0064:   return None

0194: def lt_folding(x:UOp, c:int) -> UOp|None:
0195:   p, np = partition(x.split_uop(Ops.ADD), lambda u: u.const_factor() == 1)
0196:   if np and (d:=math.gcd(*[u.const_factor() for u in np], c)) > 1 and 0 <= sum(u.vmin for u in p) and sum(u.vmax for u in p) < d:
0197:     return unwrap(UOp.usum(*np).divides(d))<(c//d)
0198:   return None

0200: def canonicalize_simplex(X:UOp) -> UOp|None:
0201:   # (X := a0*x0 + a1*x1 + ...) > 0 is equivalent to x0 + x1 + ... > 0 if xi >= 0 and ai > 0 for ints.
0202:   # returns x0 + x1 + ... in such case, or None if not
0203:   changed, ret = False, []

0205:     # assumed the const is the last src of MUL

0207:       changed = True
0208:       u = u.src[0]
0209:     if not (u.op in GroupOp.Irreducible and u.vmin >= 0): return None
0210:     ret.append(u)
0211:   return UOp.usum(*ret) if changed else None

0311: def uop_given_valid(valid:UOp, uop:UOp, try_simplex=True) -> UOp:
0312:   # return simplified uop (might be the same as input)
0313: 
0314:   # first, parse valid into {expr: (lower_bound, upper_bound)}
0315:   bounds:defaultdict[UOp, list[PyConst|None]] = defaultdict(lambda: [None, None])
0316:   for stmt in valid.split_uop(Ops.AND):
0317:     if (res:=parse_valid(stmt)) is None: continue
0318:     expr, is_upper, c = res
0319:     bounds[expr][int(is_upper)] = c
0320: 
0321:   # simplify uop given that valid is True
0322:   all_candidates = []
0323:   for i,(expr,v) in enumerate(bounds.items()):
0324:     v0, v1 = (expr.vmin if v[0] is None else v[0], expr.vmax if v[1] is None else v[1])
0325:     # try checking the whole clause
0326:     all_candidates.append((expr, UOp.variable(f"fake{i}", v0, v1, expr.dtype)))
0327: 
0328:     if try_simplex:
0329:       # every candidate is a set of constrained UOp based on valid, and if every item in a set simplifies the uop into a same output, we rewrite uop
0330:       candidates = [[all_candidates[-1]]]
0331:       if expr.op is Ops.ADD and v0 == 1 and all(u.op in GroupOp.Irreducible for u in expr.split_uop(Ops.ADD)):
0332:         # if the constraint is a simplex: X0 + X1 + ... > 0, we can check if all Xi > 0 simplify into the same output
0333:         candidates.append([(Xi, UOp.variable(f"fake{i}", 1, Xi.vmax, Xi.dtype)) for Xi in expr.split_uop(Ops.ADD)])
0334: 
0335:       for candidate in candidates:
0336:         # if every branch in candidate gives the same simplified uop, we can rewrite the uop
0337:         newuops = [uop.substitute({X:newX}) for X,newX in candidate]
0338:         if any(u is uop for u in newuops): continue  # if any branch doesnt appear in uop, skip
0339:         newuops = [u.simplify().substitute({newX:X}).simplify() for (X,newX),u in zip(candidate,newuops)]
0340:         if all_same(newuops): uop = newuops[0]
0341:         elif uop.op is Ops.STACK and len(uop.src) == 2:
0342:           if all_same([uops.src[0] for uops in newuops]): uop = uop.replace(src=(newuops[0].src[0], uop.src[1]))
0343:           if all_same([uops.src[1] for uops in newuops]): uop = uop.replace(src=(uop.src[0], newuops[0].src[1]))
0344: 
0345:   # try all the valids together (but only the whole expressions)
0346:   if (s_uop:=uop.substitute(sub_dict:=dict(all_candidates))) is not uop:
0347:     uop = s_uop.simplify().substitute({newX:X for X,newX in sub_dict.items()}).simplify()
0348:   return uop

0040: 
0041:   def calc_stats(self, x:Tensor) -> tuple[Tensor, Tensor]:
0042:     shape_mask: list[int] = [1, -1, *([1]*(x.ndim-2))]
0043:     if self.track_running_stats and not TRAINING: return self.running_mean, self.running_var.reshape(shape=shape_mask).expand(x.shape)
0044:     # This requires two full memory accesses to x
0045:     # https://github.com/pytorch/pytorch/blob/c618dc13d2aa23625cb0d7ada694137532a4fa33/aten/src/ATen/native/cuda/Normalization.cuh
0046:     # There's "online" algorithms that fix this, like https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Algorithms_for_calculating_variance#Welford's_Online_algorithm
0047:     batch_mean = x.mean(axis=(reduce_axes:=tuple(x for x in range(x.ndim) if x != 1)))
0048:     y = (x - batch_mean.detach().reshape(shape=shape_mask))  # d(var)/d(mean) = 0
0049:     batch_var = (y*y).mean(axis=reduce_axes)
0050:     return batch_mean, batch_var

0052:   def __call__(self, x:Tensor) -> Tensor:

0010: class RandMixin(OpMixin):
0011:   @staticmethod
0012:   def _threefry_random_bits(key, counts0, counts1):
0013:     x = (counts1.cast(dtypes.uint64) << 32) | counts0.cast(dtypes.uint64)
0014:     x = x.threefry((key[1]._broadcast_to(x.shape).cast(dtypes.uint64) << 32) | key[0]._broadcast_to(x.shape).cast(dtypes.uint64))
0015:     return (x & 0xffffffff).cast(dtypes.uint32).cat(((x >> 32) & 0xffffffff).cast(dtypes.uint32))
0016: 
0017:   @classmethod
0018:   def random_bits(cls, key:Self, counter:Self, num:int) -> Self:
0019:     low, high = counter[0:1], counter[1:2]
0020:     bits = []
0021:     for i in range(0, num, dtypes.uint32.max):
0022:       chunk_num = min(num - i, dtypes.uint32.max)
0023:       c_low = low + (i & 0xffffffff)
0024:       c_high = high + (i >> 32) + (c_low < low).cast(dtypes.uint32)
0025:       new_key = cls._threefry_random_bits(key, c_low, c_high)
0026:       counts0 = cls.arange(ceildiv(chunk_num, 2), dtype=dtypes.uint32)
0027:       counts1 = counts0 + ceildiv(chunk_num, 2)
0028:       bits.append(cls._threefry_random_bits(new_key, counts0, counts1)[:chunk_num])
0029:     return bits[0].cat(*bits[1:]) if bits else counter[0:0]
0030: 
0031:   @staticmethod
0032:   def _bits_to_rand(bits, shape:tuple[int, ...], dtype:DType):
0033:     _, nmant = dtypes.finfo(dtype)
0034:     uint_dtype = {1: dtypes.uint8, 2: dtypes.uint16, 4: dtypes.uint32, 8: dtypes.uint64}[dtype.itemsize]
0035:     uint_bits = bits.bitcast(uint_dtype)
0036:     float_one_bits = uint_bits.const_like(1).cast(dtype).bitcast(uint_dtype)
0037:     return uint_bits.rshift(dtype.bitsize - nmant).bitwise_or(float_one_bits).bitcast(dtype)[:prod(shape)].sub(1).reshape(shape)
0038: 
0039:   @classmethod
0040:   def _rand(cls, key:Self, counter:Self, shape:tuple[int, ...], dtype:DType, contiguous:bool=True) -> Self:
0041:     bits = cls.random_bits(key, counter, ceildiv(prod(shape) * dtype.itemsize, 4))
0042:     out = cls._bits_to_rand(bits, shape, dtype)
0043:     return out.contiguous() if contiguous else out

0034:     uint_dtype = {1: dtypes.uint8, 2: dtypes.uint16, 4: dtypes.uint32, 8: dtypes.uint64}[dtype.itemsize]
0035:     uint_bits = bits.bitcast(uint_dtype)
0036:     float_one_bits = uint_bits.const_like(1).cast(dtype).bitcast(uint_dtype)
0037:     return uint_bits.rshift(dtype.bitsize - nmant).bitwise_or(float_one_bits).bitcast(dtype)[:prod(shape)].sub(1).reshape(shape)

0567:     # repeats such that we don't need padding
0568:     x = self.repeat([1] * len(noop) + [ceildiv(k * (i * f + d), i) for k, i, d, f in zip(k_, i_, d_, f_)])
0569:     # handle dilation

0572:     # handle stride

0578:   def unfold(self, dim:int, size, step:int) -> Self:
0579:     """
0580:     Unfolds the tensor along dimension `dim` into overlapping windows.
0581: 
0582:     Each window has length `size` and begins every `step` elements of `self`.
0583:     Returns the input tensor with dimension `dim` replaced by dims `(n_windows, size)`
0584:     where `n_windows = (self.shape[dim] - size) // step + 1`.
0585: 
0586:     ```python exec="true" source="above" session="tensor" result="python"
0587:     unfolded = Tensor.arange(8).unfold(0,2,2)
0588:     print("\\n".join([repr(x.numpy()) for x in unfolded]))
0589:     ```
0590:     ```python exec="true" source="above" session="tensor" result="python"
0591:     unfolded = Tensor.arange(27).reshape(3,3,3).unfold(-1,2,3)
0592:     print("\\n".join([repr(x.numpy()) for x in unfolded]))
0593:     ```
0594:     """
0595:     if size < 0: raise RuntimeError(f'size must be >= 0 but got {size=}')
0596:     if step <= 0: raise RuntimeError(f'step must be > 0 but got {step=}')
0597:     if size > self.shape[dim]: raise RuntimeError(f'maximum size for tensor at dimension {dim} is {self.shape[dim]} but size is {size}')
0598:     dim = self._resolve_dim(dim)
0599:     perm_to_last = tuple(i for i in range(self.ndim) if i != dim) + (dim,)
0600:     return self.permute(perm_to_last)._pool((size,), step).permute(argsort(perm_to_last) + (self.ndim,))

0204: class LegacyDDPMDiscretization:
0205:   def __init__(self, linear_start:float=0.00085, linear_end:float=0.0120, num_timesteps:int=1000):
0206:     self.num_timesteps = num_timesteps
0207:     betas = np.linspace(linear_start**0.5, linear_end**0.5, num_timesteps, dtype=np.float32) ** 2
0208:     alphas = 1.0 - betas
0209:     self.alphas_cumprod = np.cumprod(alphas, axis=0)
0210: 
0211:   def __call__(self, n:int, flip:bool=False) -> Tensor:
0212:     if n < self.num_timesteps:
0213:       timesteps = np.linspace(self.num_timesteps - 1, 0, n, endpoint=False).astype(int)[::-1]
0214:       alphas_cumprod = self.alphas_cumprod[timesteps]
0215:     elif n == self.num_timesteps:
0216:       alphas_cumprod = self.alphas_cumprod
0217:     sigmas = Tensor((1 - alphas_cumprod) / alphas_cumprod) ** 0.5
0218:     sigmas = Tensor.cat(Tensor.zeros((1,)), sigmas)
0219:     return sigmas if flip else sigmas.flip(axis=0) # sigmas is "pre-flipped", need to do oposite of flag

0008: def hand_coded_optimizations(k:Scheduler) -> Scheduler:
0009:   # first try the tensor cores
0010:   """ Attempts to apply a tensor core optimization to the kernel. If one exists and applies properly, return true, otherwise return false.
0011:   Tensor cores are optimized instructions that matrix multiply-accumulate across a wave of threads: D(M, N) = A(M, K) * B(K, N) + C(M, N).
0012: 
0013:   Keyword arguments:
0014:   use_tensor_cores -- controls how tensor cores are applied (default 1)
0015:     0: will disable any tensor core matching
0016:     1: enable tensor cores
0017:     2: apply tensor core shape but don't use UOp.WMMA
0018:   extra_opts -- additional Opt's to apply after the tensor core instead of the hand-coded additional Opt's (default None)
0019:   tc_select -- specifies which tensor core(s) to use for optimization (default -1)
0020:     -1: iterates through all available tensor cores in order and uses the first one that matches the requirements (dims and dtypes)
0021:     [0-N]: uses only the n'th tensor core available; useful for search
0022:   tc_opt -- controls which kinds of kernels may be eligible for tensor cores application (default 2 during BEAM, 0 otherwise)
0023:     0: applies to only kernels with a single reduce axis and direct Ops.LOAD into Ops.MUL
0024:     1: allows kernels with multiple reduce axes and also multiplication of Ops.CAST'd buffers
0025:     2: allows kernels with M, N, K axes that are not multiples of the tensor core dimensions by applying padding those axes as needed
0026:   """
0027:   # NOTE: unless TC_OPT is > 0, we only trigger tensor cores if there's only one reduce axis
0028:   if USE_TC > 0 and (len(k.axes_of(AxisType.GROUP_REDUCE, AxisType.REDUCE)) == 1 or (TC_OPT.value >= 1)):
0029:     good_tc_opt = False
0030:     tk = k.copy()
0031:     try: # check TC first and apply hand-coded opts if successful
0032:       rngs = tk.apply_opt(Opt(OptOps.TC, 0, (TC_SELECT.value, TC_OPT.value, USE_TC.value)))
0033:       good_tc_opt = True
0034:     except KernelOptError:
0035:       pass
0036:     if good_tc_opt:
0037:       if rngs is not None:
0038:         for tc_dim in [1,0]: # attempt to upcast M and N
0039:           szs = [sz for sz in [5,4,3,2] if rngs[tc_dim].src[0].divides(sz) is not None]
0040:           if szs:
0041:             # set it to the replaced range
0042:             rngs[tc_dim] = tk.apply_opt(Opt(OptOps.UPCAST, tk.rngs.index(rngs[tc_dim]), szs[0]))[0]
0043:         if (szs := [sz for sz in [4,2] if rngs[0].src[0].divides(sz) is not None]): # attempt to local N
0044:           tk.apply_opt(Opt(OptOps.LOCAL, tk.rngs.index(rngs[0]), szs[0]))
0045:       return tk
0046: 
0047:   # make a copy so it does not mutate the input
0048:   k = k.copy()
0049: 
0050:   # upcast float4 images, this must be early so we don't accidentally add locals before the upcast
0051:   if IMAGE:
0052:     for buf_index,buf in enumerate(k.bufs):
0053:       if image_valid_dims(buf.src[0].dtype.base, buf.src[0].max_numel(), k.ren.target.arch):
